reviews.review:
You should play this game if you:

1. Are a Warhammer 40k fan.
2. Are a Relic fan.
3. Like to fight in power armor that makes Ironman look like a real ♥♥♥♥♥.
4. Like to mass murder science fiction equivalents of Orcs.
5. Like themes that cater to excessive, impractical and utterly inefficient but badass technology.
6. Like to skip guns and jam a chainsword into someone's mouth.
7. Dream of being a Space Marine.
8. Dream of being a elite badass with no equal.
9. Like to join friends and fight waves of enemies for no particular reason.
10. Enjoy seeing purity seals, incense and skull probes.
11. All of the Above.
12. Any combination of the above.

If you don't like this game, then you:

1. Are a HERETIC!
2. Can't tolerate impractical and badass technology.
3. Are a ♥♥♥♥♥ who likes Ironman.
4. Exocommunicate Traitoris.
5. Are all of the above.
6. Any combination of the above.
7. This listing has been deleted by order of the Inquisition.

This was actually the first game I added to my wishlist, way back when I decided to start using wishlists more. Got it through the humble bundle with a bunch of Warhammer games, and I was actually pretty excited to finally get down to playing it. Something about satisfying the longstanding #1 on my wishlist.

Ultimately, Space Marine is a good exploration of the 40k universe, but the campaign leaves a bit to be desired. The only time you'll die is when the game gets lucky and a bunch of long range enemies start landing shots on you in succession. It leads to really frustrating moments, over and over again, and they seem to exponentially increase as the campaign goes on. Near the end you'll have all sorts of laser-aim enemies hitting you with all sorts of BS that seems to kill you before you can respond adequately.

I had a good time with it, and I expect to get a few more hours out of the multiplayer - which includes a horde cooperative mode and a PVP mode, and both seem to be a really fun time with people still playing as of August 2015 - but I can't endorse paying more than the sale price of $7.50 for it.
I haven't had a game I couldn't put down since MW2. This gameplay is what Gears of War should have been. I am personally holding all of you responsible for not telling me about this game earlier.
